experiment: C6 exploratory two-level hierarchical recursive Canaria recompilation
observations: Strict depth-2 recursion without returning to the original full-span target completed in all 3 seeds but accumulated a substantial functional penalty: per-seed final/direct NMSE ratios 1.7433x to 1.9637x.
Jointly adapting the recursively generated C12+C34 hierarchy to the original full span before re-freezing reduced final/direct ratios to 1.1812x to 1.2315x.
Hierarchical joint adaptation beat the single-level recursive baseline in final original-teacher NMSE in all 3 exploratory seeds.
The hierarchy retained the same 4096 learned-parameter budget at the local, pair, and final levels.
No held-out test outcome was evaluated.
interpretation: Two-level recursive Canaria compilation is numerically viable in this residual-MLP testbed, but strict recursion accumulates error. A freeze/unfreeze boundary operation at the second hierarchy level substantially repairs that accumulation and, in these exploratory seeds, outperforms a one-level recursive baseline. Fresh confirmatory testing is required before a depth-2 public claim.
